note: Thresholds set by Tom (RL-IND-1 and 2 on 16 Nov 2026, RL-IND-3 and 4 on 18 Nov 2026): an item that meets one is tier anomaly with a baseline_ref (relief/feed.py rule(); check recomputes it). No warning problem yet, so no item carries an indicator_id (the contract would then need a hypothesis); the indicator is named in the item's summary and baseline_ref id.

indicators.text: A country has more IFRC appeals starting in the last 90 days than its own ten-year rate makes likely.
indicators.rule: set 16 Nov 2026 (Tom): an appeal that started in the last 90 days, in a country whose count in those 90 days is at least 2 and whose Poisson tail probability of at least that count, at the country's mean per 90 days over the ten years before the window, is below 0.01

indicators.text: WHO publishes an outbreak notice naming a country it has not named in the two years before.
indicators.rule: set 16 Nov 2026 (Tom): prior_notices_730_days is 0 for a country in the notice (only when WHO's read reaches back the whole 730 days)

indicators.text: A country's UN-coordinated plan counts far more people in need than last year's plan for that country.
indicators.rule: set 18 Nov 2026 (Tom): the intersectoral people in need in the country's current plan (OCHA HPC via HDX HAPI) is at least 25% above the figure in its plan for the year before

indicators.text: ReliefWeb posts far more reports on a disaster, or on a country, in a week than its own recent record makes likely.
indicators.rule: set 18 Nov 2026 (Tom): at least 10 ReliefWeb reports in the last 7 days on the disaster (or with the country as main country), and a Poisson tail probability of at least that many below 0.01 at its mean per week over the 12 weeks before
